docs.title: nowcastrenewal
docs.text:
Renewal models of an outbreak, built on PyRenew: the fitted renewal models and the joint model that simulates outbreaks.

nowcastrenewal is the package in packages/nowcastrenewal of the repository (Packages).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv pip install "git+https://github.com/seabbs/bdbv-hub-modelling#subdirectory=packages/nowcastrenewal"

The fitted renewal model also needs PyRenew, the model extra.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
The fitted models and the simulator share one set of components. Each delay is a continuous distribution recorded on whole days, so its pmf is double interval censored. Here we make the generation time from its mean and coefficient of variation.

import numpy as np

from nowcastrenewal.components.pmfs import (
    Delay,
    delay_pmf,
    generation_time_pmf,
)

gt = generation_time_pmf(Delay.from_mean_cv("gamma", 15.3, 9.3 / 15.3), 42)
# PyRenew's convention: element 0 is a lag of one day.
assert gt.shape == (42,)
assert np.isclose(gt.sum(), 1.0)
incubation = delay_pmf(Delay.from_mean_cv("lognormal", 6.3, 3.5 / 6.3), 28)
assert incubation.shape == (29,)

run_renewal runs each place's renewal from starting infections and reproduction numbers. We run two places for 60 days, one growing and one shrinking.

from nowcastrenewal.components.renewal import run_renewal

n_days, n_places = 60, 2
start = np.full((len(gt), n_places), 5.0)
rt = np.tile([1.3, 0.8], (n_days, 1))
run = run_renewal(start, gt, rt, population=[1e6, 1e6])
# The starting infections, then one row a day.
assert run.infections.shape == (len(gt) + n_days, n_places)
assert run.infections[-1, 0] > run.infections[-1, 1]

Next: How to.

docs.title: Mix infections between places
docs.text:
A kernel says where each place's contacts go, and a share says how much of its force of infection leaves. mixing_matrix turns them into the matrix the renewal uses. Here the kernel decays with the distance between the two places.

from nowcastrenewal.components.mixing import (
    distance_kernel,
    great_circle_km,
    mixing_matrix,
)

km = great_circle_km([0.0, 0.5], [20.0, 20.5])
kernel = distance_kernel(km, decay=50.0, per="origin")
mixing = mixing_matrix(kernel, share=0.1)
# Each origin keeps 90% and sends 10% to the other place.
assert np.allclose(mixing, [[0.9, 0.1], [0.1, 0.9]])
mixed = run_renewal(start, gt, rt, population=[1e6, 1e6], mixing=mixing)
# The shrinking place now takes in infections from the growing one.
assert mixed.infections[-1, 1] > run.infections[-1, 1]

docs.title: Turn infections into expected onsets
docs.text:
delayed_events convolves each place's infections with a delay and scales them by the ascertainment.

from nowcastrenewal.components.reference import delayed_events

infections = run.infections[len(gt) :]
onsets = delayed_events(infections, incubation, ascertainment=0.6)
assert onsets.shape == infections.shape

docs.title: Write a delay as hazards
docs.text:
The fitted models parametrise a reporting delay by its daily hazards of report. log_hazard_probs turns logit hazards back into log probabilities.

from nowcastrenewal.components.hazards import log_hazard_probs
from nowcastrenewal.components.pmfs import censored_logit_hazard, censored_pmf

report = Delay.from_mean_cv("gamma", 3.0, 0.8)
pmf = censored_pmf(report, 10)
log_p = log_hazard_probs(censored_logit_hazard(report, 10))
assert np.allclose(np.exp(log_p), pmf, atol=1e-6)

docs.title: Look up the model variants
docs.text:
The hub models are variants of one configuration (ModelConfig). renewalbvd adds the BVDOutbreakSize reproduction numbers as a pseudo-observation.

from nowcastrenewal.forecaster import VARIANTS, model_config

assert list(VARIANTS) == ["renewal", "renewalsp", "renewalbvd"]
assert model_config(VARIANTS["renewalbvd"]).bvd
assert not model_config(VARIANTS["renewal"]).bvd

The model's fixed delays come from the same pmfs.

from nowcastrenewal.model.model import (
    generation_interval,
    incubation_period,
    seed_lead,
)

assert np.allclose(generation_interval(), gt)
# Days to seed a place before its first case week.
assert seed_lead(incubation_period()) == 5

docs.title: Choose a BVDOutbreakSize release
docs.text:
A forecast may use a BVDOutbreakSize release only if it existed at the forecast's cut-off. bvd_cutoff gives that time, and parse_releases keeps the results-<run> releases from the GitHub release list.

from nowcastrenewal.bvd import bvd_cutoff, parse_releases

cutoff = bvd_cutoff("2026-10-24")
assert cutoff.isoformat() == "2026-10-25T23:59:59+01:00"
payload = [
    {"tag_name": "results-3169", "published_at": "2026-10-27T10:00:00Z"},
    {"tag_name": "latest", "published_at": "2026-10-27T10:00:00Z"},
]
releases = parse_releases(payload)
assert list(releases["tag"]) == ["results-3169"]

select_release then picks the newest of them that qualifies.

docs.title: nowcastrenewal.bvd
docs.text:
Reproduction number estimates published by BVDOutbreakSize.

The renewalbvd variant uses the latest posterior estimates of the main BVDOutbreakSize model. They come from its public results-<run> GitHub releases, one per docs build.

A forecast may use a release only if it existed at the forecast's cut-off. So select_release takes the newest results-<run> release that was published, with every asset last updated, by the cut-off, and whose data end (as_of) on or before the forecast date. Builds are republished on old data with newer code, so as_of alone is not enough: results-3169, published on 27 October with as_of 20 October, must not feed the 24 October vintage.

The release must also come from a fit that converged, under a generous check: the joint fit's worst R-hat at most MAX_RHAT (1.1, the config value [bvd] max_rhat), with effective sample sizes ignored. The releases carry no diagnostics asset. The rendered site (site.zip) does, as the fit diagnostics table: summary_assets/diagnostics.html from 17 September, and the analysis page before that. A release whose table cannot be read does not qualify, and the next older one is tried. site.zip is large, so it is downloaded once, only for a release that is otherwise eligible, and only the R-hat is kept.

Each release is cached by tag. load_release returns plain arrays: the national R_T draws on the log scale and, where the release has province estimates, each BVD patch with the hub provinces it covers. Releases before 23 October have no province_estimates.csv asset, and are national only here.

BVDOutbreakSize results are MIT licensed. Cite them as https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20312758.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReleaseChoice:
    """The release a forecast uses, and why newer ones were not.

    Attributes
    ----------
    tag : str
        The release tag.
    joint_max_rhat : float
        The joint fit's worst R-hat.
    max_rhat : float
        The limit it was held to.
    skipped : tuple of (str, str)
        Each newer release published by the cut-off, with the reason it
        was not used, newest first.
    """

    tag: str
    joint_max_rhat: float
    max_rhat: float
    skipped: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()

    def record(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the choice as plain JSON values.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            `tag`, `joint_max_rhat`, `max_rhat` and `skipped`, a list of
            `tag` and `reason` mappings.
        """
        return {
            "tag": self.tag,
            "joint_max_rhat": self.joint_max_rhat,
            "max_rhat": self.max_rhat,
            "skipped": [{"tag": t, "reason": r} for t, r in self.skipped],
        }

def parse_releases(payload: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy the GitHub release list of BVDOutbreakSize.

    Parameters
    ----------
    payload : list of mapping
        Releases as the GitHub REST API returns them.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per published `results-<run>` release, newest publication
        first, with `tag`, `published_at` (UTC) and `assets`, a mapping
        from asset name to its download URL and `updated_at`.
    """
    rows = []
    for rel in payload:
        tag = str(rel["tag_name"])
        if rel.get("draft") or not RESULTS_TAG.match(tag):
            continue
        if not rel.get("published_at"):
            continue
        assets = {
            str(a["name"]): {
                "url": str(a["browser_download_url"]),
                "updated_at": pd.Timestamp(a["updated_at"]),
            }
            for a in rel.get("assets", [])
        }
        rows.append((tag, pd.Timestamp(rel["published_at"]), assets))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["tag", "published_at", "assets"])
    out["published_at"] = pd.to_datetime(out["published_at"], utc=True)
    return out.sort_values("published_at", ascending=False).reset_index(
        drop=True
    )

def list_releases(
    token: str | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:  # pragma: no cover - network
    """List the `results-<run>` releases of BVDOutbreakSize.

    Parameters
    ----------
    token : str, optional
        A GitHub token, for the API rate limit; by default
        `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` from the environment.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        See `parse_releases`.
    """
    token = (
        token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN")
    )
    payload: list[Mapping[str, Any]] = []
    page = 1
    while True:
        url = (
            f"https://api.github.com/repos/{BVD_REPO}/releases"
            f"?per_page=100&page={page}"
        )
        headers = {"User-Agent": "bdbv-hub-modelling"}
        if token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            batch = json.loads(resp.read())
        if not batch:
            break
        payload.extend(batch)
        page += 1
    return parse_releases(payload)

def save_releases(releases: pd.DataFrame, cache_dir: Path | str) -> Path:
    """Write a release list to the cache.

    Parameters
    ----------
    releases : pandas.DataFrame
        From `parse_releases`.
    cache_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The cache.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The file written.
    """
    rows = [
        {
            "tag": str(tag),
            "published_at": pd.Timestamp(pub).isoformat(),
            "assets": {
                name: {
                    "url": str(a["url"]),
                    "updated_at": pd.Timestamp(a["updated_at"]).isoformat(),
                }
                for name, a in assets.items()
                if name in TIMED_ASSETS
            },
        }
        for tag, pub, assets in zip(
            releases["tag"],
            releases["published_at"],
            releases["assets"],
            strict=True,
        )
    ]
    path = Path(cache_dir) / RELEASES_FILE
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=1) + "\n")
    return path

def load_releases(cache_dir: Path | str) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    """Read the cached release list.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cache_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The cache.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame or None
        As `parse_releases`, keeping only the assets in `TIMED_ASSETS`, or
        None if there is no cached list.
    """
    path = Path(cache_dir) / RELEASES_FILE
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    rows = json.loads(path.read_text())
    payload = [
        {
            "tag_name": r["tag"],
            "published_at": r["published_at"],
            "assets": [
                {
                    "name": name,
                    "browser_download_url": a["url"],
                    "updated_at": a["updated_at"],
                }
                for name, a in r["assets"].items()
            ],
        }
        for r in rows
    ]
    return parse_releases(payload)

def bvd_cutoff(vintage: dt.date | str) -> dt.datetime:
    """Return the time by which a release must exist to feed a vintage.

    The end of the Sunday that opens the vintage's submission window, in
    Kinshasa time, or the end of the vintage's own day if that is later.

    Parameters
    ----------
    vintage : datetime.date or str
        The data vintage.

    Returns
    -------
    datetime.datetime
        An aware datetime in `HUB_TIMEZONE`.
    """
    opens, _ = submission_window(reference_date_for_vintage(vintage))
    sunday = dt.datetime.combine(
        opens.date(), dt.time(23, 59, 59), HUB_TIMEZONE
    )
    own = dt.datetime.combine(
        pd.Timestamp(vintage).date(), dt.time(23, 59, 59), HUB_TIMEZONE
    )
    return max(sunday, own)

def select_release(
    releases: pd.DataFrame,
    forecast_date: dt.date | str,
    cutoff: dt.datetime,
    as_of: Callable[[str], dt.date | str | None],
    rhat: Callable[[str], float | None],
    max_rhat: float = MAX_RHAT,
) -> ReleaseChoice | None:
    """Choose the release a forecast may use.

    The newest release, by publication, that was published and whose
    used assets (`TIMED_ASSETS`) were last updated by `cutoff`, whose
    data end on or before `forecast_date`, and whose joint fit's worst
    R-hat is at most `max_rhat`. Releases published after `cutoff` did
    not exist for the forecast and are not recorded as skipped.

    Parameters
    ----------
    releases : pandas.DataFrame
        From `parse_releases`.
    forecast_date : datetime.date or str
        The forecast's data vintage.
    cutoff : datetime.datetime
        An aware datetime, usually `bvd_cutoff(forecast_date)`.
    as_of : callable
        Returns a release's data cut-off from its tag, or None if it is
        unknown. Only called for releases published in time.
    rhat : callable
        Returns a release's joint R-hat from its tag, or None if it
        cannot be read. Only called for releases that are otherwise
        eligible.
    max_rhat : float
        The R-hat limit.

    Returns
    -------
    ReleaseChoice or None
        The choice, or None if no release qualifies.
    """
    limit = pd.Timestamp(cutoff).tz_convert("UTC")
    day = pd.Timestamp(forecast_date).date()
    ordered = releases.sort_values("published_at", ascending=False)
    skipped: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for tag, published, assets in zip(
        ordered["tag"], ordered["published_at"], ordered["assets"], strict=True
    ):
        tag = str(tag)
        if pd.Timestamp(published) > limit:
            continue
        updated = [
            pd.Timestamp(a["updated_at"])
            for name, a in assets.items()
            if name in TIMED_ASSETS
        ]
        if any(t > limit for t in updated):
            skipped.append((tag, "an asset was updated after the cut-off"))
            continue
        data_end = as_of(tag)
        if data_end is None:
            skipped.append((tag, "no data cut-off"))
            continue
        end = pd.Timestamp(data_end).date()
        if end > day:
            skipped.append((tag, f"data end {end}, after {day}"))
            continue
        value = rhat(tag)
        if value is None:
            skipped.append((tag, "no readable joint R-hat"))
            continue
        if value > max_rhat:
            skipped.append(
                (tag, f"joint R-hat {value:.3f} is above {max_rhat:g}")
            )
            continue
        return ReleaseChoice(tag, float(value), float(max_rhat), tuple(skipped))
    return None

def joint_rhat_from_html(html: str) -> float | None:
    """Read the joint fit's worst R-hat from a rendered diagnostics table.

    The first table with `fit` and `max_rhat` header cells and a `joint`
    row. Columns are found by name, so the row-number and column-type
    rows of older pages are ignored.

    Parameters
    ----------
    html : str
        A rendered page.

    Returns
    -------
    float or None
        The R-hat, or None if no such table or value is found.
    """
    parser = _Tables()
    parser.feed(html)
    for table in parser.tables:
        for i, header in enumerate(table):
            if "fit" not in header or "max_rhat" not in header:
                continue
            fit, col = header.index("fit"), header.index("max_rhat")
            for row in table[i + 1 :]:
                if len(row) > max(fit, col) and row[fit] == "joint":
                    try:
                        return float(row[col])
                    except ValueError:
                        return None
    return None

def joint_rhat_from_site(site: bytes) -> tuple[float | None, str]:
    """Read the joint fit's worst R-hat from a release's `site.zip`.

    Pages are tried in the order of `DIAGNOSTICS_PAGES`. Bundled script
    chunks under `assets/` are not pages and are skipped.

    Parameters
    ----------
    site : bytes
        The zip archive.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        The R-hat and the page it came from, or None and the reason it
        could not be read.
    """
    try:
        archive = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(site))
    except zipfile.BadZipFile:
        return None, "site.zip is not a zip archive"
    with archive:
        names = [n for n in archive.namelist() if "/assets/" not in n]
        for page in DIAGNOSTICS_PAGES:
            for name in sorted(n for n in names if n.endswith(page)):
                html = archive.read(name).decode("utf-8", "replace")
                value = joint_rhat_from_html(html)
                if value is not None:
                    return value, name
    return None, "site.zip has no fit diagnostics table with a joint row"

def fetch_diagnostics(
    tag: str,
    assets: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]],
    cache_dir: Path | str,
    download: Downloader = _download,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read a release's joint R-hat once, into `cache_dir/<tag>/`.

    `site.zip` is downloaded, read and dropped. Only the value is kept,
    in `DIAGNOSTICS_FILE`, so a release is never downloaded twice.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tag : str
        The release tag.
    assets : mapping
        Asset name to its `url`, as in `parse_releases`.
    cache_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The cache.
    download : callable
        Returns the bytes at a URL.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `joint_max_rhat` (float or None), `source` (the page read, or
        None) and `reason` (why there is no value, or None).
    """
    path = Path(cache_dir) / tag / DIAGNOSTICS_FILE
    if path.exists():
        cached: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(path.read_text())
        return cached
    if SITE_ASSET in assets:
        value, where = joint_rhat_from_site(
            download(str(assets[SITE_ASSET]["url"]))
        )
    else:
        value, where = None, "the release has no site.zip"
    record = {
        "joint_max_rhat": value,
        "source": where if value is not None else None,
        "reason": None if value is not None else where,
    }
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=1) + "\n")
    return record

def fetch_release(
    tag: str,
    assets: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]],
    cache_dir: Path | str,
    download: Downloader = _download,
) -> Path:
    """Download a release's assets once, into `cache_dir/<tag>/`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tag : str
        The release tag.
    assets : mapping
        Asset name to its `url`, as in `parse_releases`. Only `ASSETS`
        are fetched, and only those the release has.
    cache_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The cache. A file already there is not downloaded again. Of
        `observations.toml` only `as_of_date` is kept.
    download : callable
        Returns the bytes at a URL.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The release's directory.
    """
    out = Path(cache_dir) / tag
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for name in ASSETS:
        path = out / name
        if name in assets and not path.exists():
            content = download(str(assets[name]["url"]))
            if name == "observations.toml":
                # The input data are large; only the cut-off is used.
                found = _find_key(tomllib.loads(content.decode()), "as_of_date")
                content = f'as_of_date = "{found}"\n'.encode()
            path.write_bytes(content)
    return out

def release_as_of(path: Path | str) -> dt.date | None:
    """Read a cached release's data cut-off.

    From `province_estimates.csv` where present, otherwise from the
    `as_of_date` in `observations.toml`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        The release's directory.

    Returns
    -------
    datetime.date or None
        The cut-off, or None if neither file gives it.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    est = path / "province_estimates.csv"
    if est.exists():
        return pd.Timestamp(pd.read_csv(est)["as_of"].iloc[0]).date()
    obs = path / "observations.toml"
    if obs.exists():
        found = _find_key(tomllib.loads(obs.read_text()), "as_of_date")
        if found is not None:
            return pd.Timestamp(found).date()
    return None

def load_release(path: Path | str) -> BvdRelease:
    """Read a cached release into plain arrays.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        The release's directory, named by its tag.

    Returns
    -------
    BvdRelease
        The national draws and any patch estimates.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the cut-off cannot be read, or a patch is an unknown province.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    as_of = release_as_of(path)
    if as_of is None:
        raise ValueError(f"No data cut-off in BVDOutbreakSize release {path}.")
    draws = pd.read_csv(path / "posterior_draws.csv")
    if "R_T" in draws:
        log_rt = np.log(draws["R_T"].to_numpy(dtype=float))
    else:
        # Early builds publish the growth rate only. With a Gamma
        # generation interval, R = (1 + r theta)^k (Wallinga and Lipsitch).
        k = (BVD_GI_MEAN / BVD_GI_SD) ** 2
        theta = BVD_GI_SD**2 / BVD_GI_MEAN
        log_rt = k * np.log1p(draws["r"].to_numpy(dtype=float) * theta)
    est = path / "province_estimates.csv"
    patches = _patches(pd.read_csv(est)) if est.exists() else {}
    return BvdRelease(
        tag=path.name,
        as_of=as_of,
        national_log_rt=log_rt,
        patches=patches,
        reference=_reference(path / "province_timeseries.csv", as_of),
    )

def model_rows(release: BvdRelease) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Turn a release into the rows the model's BVD term reads.

    The national row is the mean and SD of the national log `R_T` draws.
    Each patch row is its log median and log-scale SD, with the national
    row of the same table as its reference, so the deviation uses one
    source. Without that table, the national draws are the reference.

    Parameters
    ----------
    release : BvdRelease
        From `load_release`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `MODEL_ROW_COLUMNS`, the national row first.
    """
    as_of = release.as_of.isoformat()
    log_rt = release.national_log_rt
    nat = (float(log_rt.mean()), float(log_rt.std(ddof=1)))
    ref = release.reference or nat
    rows = [("national", "", as_of, *nat, *nat)]
    for name, patch in release.patches.items():
        rows.append(
            (
                name,
                ";".join(patch.members),
                as_of,
                patch.log_median,
                patch.log_sd,
                *ref,
            )
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=list(MODEL_ROW_COLUMNS))

def bvd_for_vintage(
    vintage: dt.date | str,
    cache_dir: Path | str,
    releases: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    download: Downloader = _download,
    max_rhat: float | None = None,
) -> BvdRelease | None:
    """Return the BVDOutbreakSize estimates a vintage's forecast may use.

    See `select_release`. Release files and R-hat values already in the
    cache are not downloaded again.

    Parameters
    ----------
    vintage : datetime.date or str
        The data vintage, which is also the forecast date.
    cache_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The release cache.
    releases : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        From `parse_releases`. Read from the cache (`load_releases`) if
        not given, or listed from GitHub if the cache has none.
    download : callable
        Returns the bytes at a URL.
    max_rhat : float, optional
        The R-hat limit. Defaults to the one the cache was refreshed with
        (`read_max_rhat`).

    Returns
    -------
    BvdRelease or None
        The estimates, with the choice, or None if no release qualifies.
    """
    if releases is None:
        releases = load_releases(cache_dir)
    if releases is None:  # pragma: no cover - network
        releases = list_releases()
    assets = dict(zip(releases["tag"], releases["assets"], strict=True))

    def as_of(tag: str) -> dt.date | None:
        return release_as_of(
            fetch_release(tag, assets[tag], cache_dir, download)
        )

    def rhat(tag: str) -> float | None:
        value = fetch_diagnostics(tag, assets[tag], cache_dir, download)
        found = value["joint_max_rhat"]
        return None if found is None else float(found)

    limit = read_max_rhat(cache_dir) if max_rhat is None else max_rhat
    choice = select_release(
        releases, vintage, bvd_cutoff(vintage), as_of, rhat, limit
    )
    if choice is None:
        return None
    release = load_release(Path(cache_dir) / choice.tag)
    return replace(release, choice=choice)

def refresh_cache(
    cache_dir: Path | str,
    vintages: Sequence[dt.date | str],
    releases: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    download: Downloader = _download,
    max_rhat: float = MAX_RHAT,
) -> dict[str, ReleaseChoice | None]:
    """Cache the release list and the release each vintage may use.

    The R-hat limit is recorded in the cache (`GATE_FILE`), so a later fit
    that reads the cache applies the same one.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cache_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The cache, usually `data/bvd/`.
    vintages : sequence of datetime.date or str
        The data vintages.
    releases : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        From `parse_releases`. Listed from GitHub if not given.
    download : callable
        Returns the bytes at a URL.
    max_rhat : float
        The R-hat limit.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The choice for each vintage, or None.
    """
    if releases is None:  # pragma: no cover - network
        releases = list_releases()
    save_releases(releases, cache_dir)
    gate = Path(cache_dir) / GATE_FILE
    gate.write_text(json.dumps({"max_rhat": max_rhat}) + "\n")
    chosen: dict[str, ReleaseChoice | None] = {}
    for vintage in vintages:
        rel = bvd_for_vintage(vintage, cache_dir, releases, download, max_rhat)
        chosen[pd.Timestamp(vintage).date().isoformat()] = (
            None if rel is None else rel.choice
        )
    return chosen

docs.text:
The PyRenew renewal model behind the repository's interfaces.

The model itself (JAX, NumPyro, PyRenew) is in nowcastrenewal.model. It is imported lazily, so this module and the registry work without the model extra. This module owns everything around it:

  • the variants (VARIANTS), registered as models for the backtest;
  • vintage_inputs: a ForecastTask as the model's Vintage, with the leave-one-province-out mask;
  • samples_table: trajectories as the hub sample table;
  • ppc_rows, parameter_diagnostics, chain_diagnostics: the CI's ppc.json and diagnostics.json;
  • run_records: a fitted model's chain trace, sampler fields and delays;
  • delay_summary and fit_delays: each fit's learnt delay, written as delay-summary.csv beside its forecasts;
  • fit_renewal and forecast_renewal: the fit and forecast of the main and bvd fit configurations (bdbvhub.submission.fitting).

This module reads only ModelConfig, MAIN, BVD, zones.build_model, model_args, model.EXTRA_FIELDS, forecast_trajectories and adapter.vintage_from_tables from the subpackage, so a new model version drops in if it keeps those. Sampling is here (run_nuts), so the CI's sampler table applies in full.

@dataclass
class RenewalModel:
    """A renewal variant as a `ForecastModel`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    variant : Variant
        The variant.
    sampler : dict
        NUTS settings (`sampler_settings`).
    progress : pathlib.Path or None
        File to append progress lines to.
    supports_mask : bool
        The model honours `ForecastTask.mask`.
    name : str
        The variant name.
    delay_summary : pandas.DataFrame or None
        `fit_delays` of the last `forecast`.
    last_fit : RenewalFit or None
        The fit of the last `forecast`, for `write_fit_dir`. Left out of
        the representation, which keys a stored fit.
    """

    variant: Variant
    sampler: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=sampler_settings)
    progress: Path | None = None
    supports_mask: bool = field(init=False, default=True)
    reads_zones: ClassVar[bool] = True
    reads_places: ClassVar[bool] = True
    name: str = field(init=False)
    fit_diagnostics: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(
        init=False, default_factory=list
    )
    delay_summary: pd.DataFrame | None = field(init=False, default=None)
    last_fit: RenewalFit | None = field(
        init=False, default=None, repr=False, compare=False
    )

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Name the model after its variant and say if it takes a mask."""
        self.name = self.variant.name
        # A province fitted on its own cannot be forecast without its data.
        self.supports_mask = not self.variant.per_province

    def _log(self, line: str) -> None:
        if self.progress is not None:
            with self.progress.open("a") as fh:
                fh.write(line + "\n")

    def run(self, task: ForecastTask) -> RenewalRun:
        """Fit the variant to a task and draw trajectories.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.

        Returns
        -------
        RenewalRun
            The fit and its draws.
        """
        # Imported from its module, not the package, so that the fit key
        # (`bdbvhub.store.store.fit_code`) follows the builder.
        from nowcastrenewal.model.zones import build_model

        pr = engine()
        data = vintage_inputs(task, model_config(self.variant))
        config = fit_config(self.variant, data)
        model = build_model(data, config)
        s = self.sampler
        self._log(f"variant={self.name} sampling start")
        start, cpu_start = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
        run_nuts(model, data, {"seed": task.seed, **s})
        # Pulling the draws to the host waits for the sampler.
        np.asarray(next(iter(model.mcmc.get_samples().values())))
        seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        cpu_seconds = time.process_time() - cpu_start
        self._log(
            f"variant={self.name} sampling done seconds={seconds:.0f} "
            f"cpu_seconds={cpu_seconds:.0f}"
        )
        draws = {
            **pr.forecast_trajectories(
                model,
                data,
                task.n_samples,
                seed=task.seed,
                as_of=tuple(report_cutoffs(task, data)),
            ),
            "rt": pr.weekly_rt(model, data, seed=task.seed),
        }
        trace, extra, delay = run_records(model, data, data.names)
        return RenewalRun(
            self.variant,
            data,
            draws,
            trace,
            extra,
            seconds,
            cpu_seconds,
            delay,
        )

    def forecast_fit(self, task: ForecastTask) -> RenewalFit:
        """Fit the variant to a task and return the samples.

        Every variant is fitted on health zones, by
        `nowcastrenewal.zones.ZoneRenewalModel` (pooled) or
        `SingleZoneRenewalModel` (each zone on its own), which implement
        this.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            Here.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"{self.name} is fitted on health zones (nowcastrenewal.zones)."
        )

    def _run_all(self, tasks: Mapping[str, ForecastTask]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Run every task, largest first, `province_workers` at a time.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            `RenewalRun` by key, in the order of `tasks`.
        """

        def size(key: str) -> float:
            target = tasks[key].target
            own = target["location"].isin(tasks[key].locations)
            return float(target.loc[own, "total"].sum())

        order = sorted(tasks, key=size, reverse=True)
        chains = int(self.sampler.get("num_chains", 1))
        workers = province_workers(chains, len(tasks))
        if workers == 1:
            done = {key: self.run(tasks[key]) for key in order}
        else:
            context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")
            with ProcessPoolExecutor(workers, mp_context=context) as pool:
                futures = {
                    key: pool.submit(self.run, tasks[key]) for key in order
                }
                try:
                    done = {key: f.result() for key, f in futures.items()}
                except BaseException:
                    # Fail now, not after the queued fits have run.
                    pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
                    raise
        return {key: done[key] for key in tasks}

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return joint sample trajectories for a task.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `SAMPLE_COLUMNS`. With `task.report_by`, also `as_of`
            rows (`RenewalFit.as_reported`).

        Examples
        --------
        Fitting takes minutes per task on a CPU.

        >>> from bdbvhub.models import get_model
        >>> model = get_model("renewal")
        >>> samples = model.forecast(task)
        >>> model.fit_diagnostics  # divergences and R-hat of the fit
        """
        fit = self.forecast_fit(task)
        self.last_fit = fit
        self.delay_summary = fit_delays(fit, task)
        self.fit_diagnostics = [
            {"fit": key, **fit_summary(run, self.sampler)}
            for key, run in fit.runs.items()
        ]
        samples = fit.samples
        if not task.report_by:
            return samples
        later = [] if fit.as_reported is None else [fit.as_reported]
        return pd.concat(
            [samples.assign(as_of=np.nan), *later], ignore_index=True
        )

    def write_fit_dir(
        self, task: ForecastTask, fit_dir: Path | str, config_name: str
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Write the last `forecast`'s fit as the submission reads it.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task the last `forecast` ran.
        fit_dir : pathlib.Path or str
            The fit directory.
        config_name : str
            The fit configuration (`FIT_VARIANTS`), for the records.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            The `diagnostics.json` record (`write_fit_dir`).

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the model has not forecast yet.
        """
        if self.last_fit is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.name} has no fit to write.")
        return write_fit_dir(
            self.last_fit,
            task,
            self.sampler,
            fit_dir,
            variant=self.variant.name,
            config_name=config_name,
        )

def province_workers(num_chains: int, n_provinces: int) -> int:
    """Return how many provinces a per-province variant fits at once.

    `PROVINCE_WORKERS_ENV` if set, else one fit per `num_chains` cores,
    at most `MAX_PROVINCE_WORKERS`: with parallel chains (the policy's
    setting) each chain then has a core. Never more than the provinces.

    Parameters
    ----------
    num_chains : int
        Chains of each fit, run in parallel.
    n_provinces : int
        Provinces to fit.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        At least 1.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `PROVINCE_WORKERS_ENV` is not a positive integer.
    """
    env = os.environ.get(PROVINCE_WORKERS_ENV)
    if env:
        if not env.isdigit() or int(env) < 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{PROVINCE_WORKERS_ENV} must be a positive integer, "
                f"got {env!r}."
            )
        workers = int(env)
    else:
        workers = min(MAX_PROVINCE_WORKERS, usable_cpus() // max(1, num_chains))
    return max(1, min(workers, n_provinces))

def centred_min_weekly_cases(config: ModelConfig) -> float:
    r"""Return the weekly cases from which a fit's log Rt walk is centred.

    The count noise on a weekly log change in cases is about
    $1/\sqrt{n}$ for $n$ cases a week. Where it is below the prior median
    step SD of the walk, $m$ (`ModelConfig.rt_sd_lognormal`), the counts
    pin the walk's weekly changes, so its levels are sampled (centred);
    otherwise its standardised steps are (non-centred). So the cut-off
    is $1/m^2$: 69.4 cases a week for $m = 0.12$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : ModelConfig
        The configuration.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Mean weekly cases, known and imputed, over the fit's places and
        data weeks.
    """
    median = (
        0.2 if config.rt_sd_lognormal is None else config.rt_sd_lognormal[0]
    )
    return 1.0 / median**2

def fit_config(variant: Variant, data: Vintage) -> ModelConfig:
    """Build the `ModelConfig` a variant fits to one vintage with.

    The same rule for every variant: the fit's log Rt walk is centred
    where its data's mean weekly cases, known and imputed, summed over its
    places, reach `centred_min_weekly_cases`, and non-centred otherwise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    variant : Variant
        The variant.
    data : Vintage
        The vintage, with `known` and `imputed` counts.

    Returns
    -------
    nowcastrenewal.model.ModelConfig
        `model_config(variant)`, centred where the counts pin the walk.
    """
    config = model_config(variant)
    weeks = max(int(np.asarray(data.known).shape[0]), 1)
    weekly = (np.nansum(data.known) + np.nansum(data.imputed)) / weeks
    centred = bool(weekly >= centred_min_weekly_cases(config))
    return dataclasses.replace(config, centred_rt=centred)

    from numpyro.infer import NUTS, init_to_sample

    return NUTS(
        model_fn,
        target_accept_prob=float(sampler["target_accept"]),
        max_tree_depth=int(sampler["max_tree_depth"]),
        init_strategy=init_to_sample,
    )

def run_nuts(model: Any, data: Any, sampler: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
    """Fit a built model by NUTS, keeping the fields the diagnostics need.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : pyrenew.model.MultiSignalModel
        From `build_model`.
    data : nowcastrenewal.model.Vintage
        The inputs.
    sampler : mapping
        The full sampler table (`sampler_settings`), with an optional
        `thinning`.

    Returns
    -------
    pyrenew.model.MultiSignalModel
        The model, with `model.mcmc` holding the posterior.
    """
    import jax
    from jax import random
    from numpyro.infer import MCMC

    # Each fit compiles its own model, so cached executables from earlier
    # fits never help and exhaust LLVM memory over many locations.
    jax.clear_caches()  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]
    pr = engine()
    args = pr.model_args(model, data)
    model.validate_data(
        **{k: v for k, v in args.items() if k != "population_size"}
    )
    model.mcmc = MCMC(
        nuts_kernel(model.sample, sampler),
        num_warmup=int(sampler["num_warmup"]),
        num_samples=int(sampler["num_samples"]),
        num_chains=int(sampler["num_chains"]),
        # Every `thinning`-th draw is kept, so a long chain fits in memory.
        thinning=int(sampler.get("thinning", 1)),
        chain_method=str(sampler.get("chain_method", "vectorized")),
        progress_bar=False,
    )
    model.mcmc.run(
        random.key(int(sampler["seed"])),
        extra_fields=pr.model.EXTRA_FIELDS,
        **args,
    )
    return model

def bvd_record(release: BvdRelease | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Describe the BVDOutbreakSize release used, for the fit diagnostics.

    Parameters
    ----------
    release : nowcastrenewal.bvd.BvdRelease or None
        From `bvd_release`.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `tag`, `as_of`, the joint fit's `joint_max_rhat`, the `max_rhat`
        limit and the newer releases `skipped` with their reasons, or
        only `tag: None` if no release qualified.
    """
    if release is None:
        return {"tag": None}
    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "tag": release.tag,
        "as_of": release.as_of.isoformat(),
    }
    if release.choice is not None:
        record.update(release.choice.record())
    return record

def vintage_inputs(
    task: ForecastTask,
    config: Any,
    table: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    bvd: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Turn a forecast task into the model's `Vintage`.

    A thin call to the model's own `vintage_from_tables`, which chooses
    the active set (the provinces with cases) and the week grid. Provinces
    in `task.mask` have their likelihood switched off and their delays
    left out. They stay in the latent process, so they are still
    forecast.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.
    config : nowcastrenewal.model.ModelConfig
        The model configuration.
    table : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        The places (populations and centres). Defaults to the task's
        (`ForecastTask.places`).
    bvd : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        BVDOutbreakSize rows (`bvd_rows`), for a variant with the BVD
        term. Without them that variant is the main model.

    Returns
    -------
    nowcastrenewal.model.Vintage
        The model inputs.
    """
    from nowcastrenewal.model.inputs import vintage_from_tables
    from nowcastutils.releases import release_pairs

    pairs = None
    if task.delay_history is not None:
        pairs = release_pairs(task.delay_history, task.vintage)
    return vintage_from_tables(
        task.target,
        task.delays,
        task.vintage,
        tuple(task.locations),
        task_places(task) if table is None else table,
        config,
        horizon_weeks(task),
        tuple(task.mask),
        bvd=bvd,
        release_pairs=pairs,
        imputation_delay=task_imputation_delay(task),
    )

def samples_table(
    task: ForecastTask,
    data: Any,
    draws: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Province sample rows of the modelled provinces.

    Weeks before the model grid take the data in every sample.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.
    data : nowcastrenewal.model.Vintage
        The fitted inputs.
    draws : mapping
        `forecast_trajectories` output, with `province`
        `(n, n_weeks + horizon, P)`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Province samples, columns `SAMPLE_COLUMNS`.
    """
    first = data.start_date + dt.timedelta(days=6)
    rows = task.target.loc[task.target["vintage"] == task.vintage]
    observed = rows.pivot_table(
        index="target_end_date", columns="location", values="total"
    )
    n = task.n_samples
    out: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for date in task.target_end_dates:
        i = (epiweek_end(date) - first).days // 7
        for j, loc in enumerate(data.names):
            if i < 0:  # before the model grid: the data
                value = observed[loc].get(date, 0) if loc in observed else 0
                values = np.full(n, float(np.nan_to_num(value)))
            else:
                values = np.asarray(draws["province"])[:n, i, j]
            frame = pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "location": loc,
                    "target_end_date": date,
                    "sample": np.arange(1, n + 1),
                    "value": np.asarray(values, dtype=float),
                }
            )
            out.append(frame)
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True).loc[:, list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS)]

def check_national(task: ForecastTask) -> None:
    """Stop if the task's national data hold cases in no province.

    National is the sum of the provinces, sample by sample, so cases the
    hub counts nationally but in no province would be lost. No release
    has had any (`data/national-coherence.csv`), so a fit stops rather
    than guess where they belong. The submission's coherence check fails
    on the same data (`bdbvhub coherence`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If national exceeds the sum of the provinces in a week.
    """
    rows = task.target.loc[task.target["vintage"] == task.vintage]
    wide = rows.pivot_table(
        index="target_end_date", columns="location", values="total"
    ).fillna(0)
    if NATIONAL not in wide:
        return
    gap = wide[NATIONAL] - wide.drop(columns=NATIONAL).sum(axis=1)
    weeks = [str(w) for w in gap.index[gap > 0]]
    if weeks:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{task.vintage}: national cases in no province in weeks "
            f"{', '.join(weeks)}; national is the sum of the provinces."
        )

def ppc_rows(
    data: Any, insample: Mapping[str, Any]
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, NDArray[np.float64]]:
    """Observed rows and the matching in-sample predictive draws.

    One row per location, stream and data week for the streams the model
    fits (`observed` and `imputed`, or `total`), plus national rows as
    the sum of the province draws within each draw. These are the
    `observed` and `draws` arguments of
    `nowcasteval.ppc.summarise_draws`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : nowcastrenewal.model.Vintage
        The fitted inputs.
    insample : mapping
        Draws of the vintage counts by stream (`known`, `imputed` or
        `total`), each `(n_draws, n_weeks + horizon, P)`.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        `observed` (columns `location`, `stream`, `target_end_date`,
        `observed`) and `draws`, `(n_draws, len(observed))`.
    """
    first = data.start_date + dt.timedelta(days=6)
    weeks = _weeks(first, data.n_weeks)
    by_stream = {
        "known": data.known,
        "imputed": data.imputed,
        "total": data.known + data.imputed,
    }
    hub_name = {"known": "observed", "imputed": "imputed", "total": "total"}
    rows: list[tuple[str, str, str, float]] = []
    cols: list[NDArray[np.float64]] = []
    for stream, x in insample.items():
        draws = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)[:, : data.n_weeks]
        obs = by_stream[stream]
        for j, loc in enumerate(data.names):
            for i, week in enumerate(weeks):
                rows.append((loc, hub_name[stream], week, float(obs[i, j])))
                cols.append(draws[:, i, j])
        if len(data.names) > 1:
            for i, week in enumerate(weeks):
                rows.append(
                    (NATIONAL, hub_name[stream], week, float(obs[i].sum()))
                )
                cols.append(draws[:, i].sum(axis=1))
    observed = pd.DataFrame(
        rows, columns=["location", "stream", "target_end_date", "observed"]
    )
    return observed, np.column_stack(cols)

def ebfmi(energy: NDArray[np.float64]) -> float:
    r"""Energy Bayesian fraction of missing information of one chain.

    Parameters
    ----------
    energy : numpy.ndarray
        Hamiltonian energy of each draw.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        $\sum_n (E_n - E_{n-1})^2 / \sum_n (E_n - \bar E)^2$. Below 0.3
        suggests the momentum resampling explores the energy poorly.
    """
    e = np.asarray(energy, dtype=float)
    return float(np.sum(np.diff(e) ** 2) / np.sum((e - e.mean()) ** 2))

def delay_summary(
    beta: NDArray[np.floating],
    shift: NDArray[np.floating],
    first_day: dt.date,
    last_day: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    r"""Summarise a fit's onset-to-report delay over posterior draws.

    The delay pmf of onset day $s$ follows from the hazards
    $\beta(d) + \gamma(s)$ (`components.hazards.log_hazard_probs`), as in
    `HazardDelay`, from the recorded `delay_beta` and `delay_shift` draws.

    Parameters
    ----------
    beta : numpy.ndarray
        `delay_beta` draws, `(draws, dmax)`.
    shift : numpy.ndarray
        `delay_shift` draws, `(draws, days)`, on the model axis.
    first_day : datetime.date
        Date of the model axis's first day.
    last_day : int
        Index on the axis of the last onset day at the vintage.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `kind`, `x`, `quantity` and `q5`, `q50`, `q95` over the
        draws. `kind` `"cumulative"` has, by delay day `x`, the share
        reported by then (`reported_share`) for onsets in the last week.
        `kind` `"onset_week"` has, by onset week ending `x`, the median
        delay in days (`median_delay`), the mean delay in days
        (`mean_delay`) and the share reported within 7 days
        (`share_within_7`).
    """
    import jax.numpy as jnp

    from nowcastrenewal.components.hazards import log_hazard_probs

    days = pd.date_range(first_day, periods=last_day + 1, freq="D")
    # The last day of each onset week (to Saturday) up to the vintage.
    week_end = days + pd.to_timedelta((5 - days.dayofweek) % 7, unit="D")
    last = (
        pd.Series(np.arange(len(days)), index=week_end).groupby(level=0).max()
    )
    logit = beta[:, None, :] + shift[:, last.to_numpy()][:, :, None]
    pmf = jnp.exp(log_hazard_probs(jnp.asarray(logit), close=True))
    cdf = np.cumsum(np.asarray(pmf), axis=-1)
    qs = list(_DELAY_QUANTILES)

    def rows(
        values: NDArray[np.floating], x: list[Any], kind: str, name: str
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        q = np.quantile(values, qs, axis=0)
        return pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "kind": kind,
                "x": x,
                "quantity": name,
                "q5": q[0],
                "q50": q[1],
                "q95": q[2],
            }
        )

    weeks = [d.date().isoformat() for d in last.index]
    return pd.concat(
        [
            rows(
                cdf[:, -1, :],
                list(range(cdf.shape[-1])),
                "cumulative",
                "reported_share",
            ),
            rows(
                (cdf >= 0.5).argmax(axis=-1).astype(float),
                weeks,
                "onset_week",
                "median_delay",
            ),
            rows(cdf[:, :, 7], weeks, "onset_week", "share_within_7"),
            rows((1 - cdf).sum(axis=-1), weeks, "onset_week", "mean_delay"),
        ],
        ignore_index=True,
    )

        fields by chain, and the `delay_summary` rows of each place's
        delay (column `place`), with the shared delay of several places.
    """
    by_chain = model.mcmc.get_samples(group_by_chain=True)
    trace = {
        k: np.asarray(by_chain[k])
        for k in model.mcmc.last_state.z
        if k in by_chain
    }
    extra = {
        k: np.asarray(v)
        for k, v in model.mcmc.get_extra_fields(group_by_chain=True).items()
    }
    posterior = model.mcmc.get_samples()
    n_init = model.latent.n_initialization_points
    beta = np.asarray(posterior["delay_beta"])
    shifts = {
        name: np.asarray(posterior["delay_shift"])[..., p]
        for p, name in enumerate(places)
    }
    if len(shifts) > 1:
        shifts["shared"] = np.asarray(posterior["delay_shared_shift"])[..., 0]
    delay = pd.concat(
        [
            delay_summary(
                beta,
                shift,
                data.start_date - dt.timedelta(days=n_init),
                n_init + data.cutoff,
            ).assign(place=place)
            for place, shift in shifts.items()
        ],
        ignore_index=True,
    )
    return trace, extra, delay

def fit_summary(run: RenewalRun, sampler: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarise one fit: sampler settings, time and convergence.

    Parameters
    ----------
    run : RenewalRun
        The fit.
    sampler : mapping
        Its sampler settings.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `num_chains`, `num_warmup`, `num_samples`, `max_tree_depth`,
        `seconds`, `max_rhat`, `min_ess_bulk`, and the shares of draws
        that diverged (`divergent_share`) or hit the tree depth cap
        (`depth_share`).
    """
    depth = int(
        sampler.get("max_tree_depth", DEFAULT_SAMPLER["max_tree_depth"])
    )
    chains = chain_diagnostics(run.extra, depth)
    params = parameter_diagnostics(run.trace)
    rhat = [p["rhat"] for p in params if p["rhat"] is not None]
    ess = [p["ess_bulk"] for p in params if p["ess_bulk"] is not None]
    draws = sum(c["draws"] for c in chains)
    hits = sum(c.get("tree_depth_hits", 0) for c in chains)
    return {
        **{
            k: int(sampler.get(k, DEFAULT_SAMPLER[k]))
            for k in ("num_chains", "num_warmup", "num_samples")
        },
        "max_tree_depth": depth,
        "seconds": float(run.seconds),
        "max_rhat": max(rhat, default=float("nan")),
        "min_ess_bulk": min(ess, default=float("nan")),
        "divergent_share": sum(c["divergences"] for c in chains) / draws,
        "depth_share": hits / draws,
    }

def chain_diagnostics(
    extra: Mapping[str, Any], max_tree_depth: int
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Per-chain sampler diagnostics, as BVDOutbreakSize reports them.

    Parameters
    ----------
    extra : mapping
        NUTS extra fields by chain, `(n_chains, n_draws)`: `diverging`,
        and, if kept, `num_steps`, `accept_prob`, `energy` and
        `adapt_state.step_size`.
    max_tree_depth : int
        The tree depth cap.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        One row per chain: `chain`, `draws`, `divergences`, and
        `step_size`, `tree_depth_hits` (draws at the cap),
        `tree_depth_share`, `mean_accept` and `ebfmi` when available.
    """
    x = {k: np.asarray(v) for k, v in extra.items()}
    diverging = x["diverging"]
    chains = []
    for c in range(diverging.shape[0]):
        row: dict[str, Any] = {
            "chain": c,
            "draws": int(diverging.shape[1]),
            "divergences": int(diverging[c].sum()),
        }
        if "num_steps" in x:
            hits = x["num_steps"][c] >= 2**max_tree_depth - 1
            row["tree_depth_hits"] = int(hits.sum())
            row["tree_depth_share"] = float(hits.mean())
        if "adapt_state.step_size" in x:
            row["step_size"] = float(x["adapt_state.step_size"][c][-1])
        if "accept_prob" in x:
            row["mean_accept"] = float(x["accept_prob"][c].mean())
        if "energy" in x:
            row["ebfmi"] = ebfmi(x["energy"][c])
        chains.append(row)
    return chains

R-hat and effective sample sizes of every sampled scalar.

Rank-normalised split R-hat and bulk ESS, and tail ESS as the smaller ESS of the 5% and 95% quantile indicators (Vehtari et al. 2021). Undefined values, such as for a constant, are None.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default trace mapping

required

Type Description list of dict

def parameter_diagnostics(
    trace: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """R-hat and effective sample sizes of every sampled scalar.

    Rank-normalised split R-hat and bulk ESS, and tail ESS as the smaller
    ESS of the 5% and 95% quantile indicators (Vehtari et al. 2021).
    Undefined values, such as for a constant, are None.

    Parameters
    ----------
    trace : mapping
        Draws of each sampled site by chain, `(n_chains, n_draws, ...)`.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        One row per scalar element, sites in name order: `name`,
        `index` (flat, 0 for a scalar), `rhat`, `ess_bulk` and `ess_tail`.
    """
    from numpyro.diagnostics import effective_sample_size, split_gelman_rubin

    def none_if_bad(value: float) -> float | None:
        return float(value) if np.isfinite(value) else None

    params = []
    for name in sorted(trace):
        x = np.asarray(trace[name], dtype=float)
        flat = x.reshape(x.shape[0], x.shape[1], -1)
        for i in range(flat.shape[2]):
            draws = flat[:, :, i]
            row: dict[str, Any] = {"name": name, "index": i}
            if np.ptp(draws) == 0:
                row |= {"rhat": None, "ess_bulk": None, "ess_tail": None}
            else:
                z = _rank_normal(draws)
                lo, hi = np.quantile(draws, [0.05, 0.95])
                tails = [
                    effective_sample_size((draws <= q).astype(float))
                    for q in (lo, hi)
                ]
                row |= {
                    "rhat": none_if_bad(split_gelman_rubin(z)),
                    "ess_bulk": none_if_bad(effective_sample_size(z)),
                    "ess_tail": none_if_bad(min(tails)),
                }
            params.append(row)
    return params

def worst_rhat(
    params: list[dict[str, Any]], n: int = 10
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return the `n` parameters with the highest R-hat.

    Parameters
    ----------
    params : list of dict
        `parameter_diagnostics` rows.
    n : int
        How many to keep.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        The rows, worst first.
    """
    rated = [p for p in params if p["rhat"] is not None]
    return sorted(rated, key=lambda p: -float(p["rhat"]))[:n]

Each fitted place (a zone, or a province fitted on its own), each province above fitted zones and the nation take the infection weighted Rt of their fitted places (rt_observation.group_rt), draw by draw, so every level comes from joint draws. Fits of provinces on their own pair draws by index, as their samples do. Places outside the fits (silent ones) have no Rt, and so add nothing to their province or the nation. A location and week with no infections in some draw has no row.

Parameters:

The task: its target_end_dates are the weeks, by week of infection.

required runs mapping

RenewalRuns whose draws hold weekly_rt output (rt).

required

Returns:

location, target_end_date, output_type_id (RT_QUANTILES) and value.

Source code in packages/nowcastrenewal/src/nowcastrenewal/forecaster.py 
def rt_quantiles(
    task: ForecastTask, runs: Mapping[str, RenewalRun]
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Weekly effective Rt quantiles of every place a fit models.

    Each fitted place (a zone, or a province fitted on its own), each
    province above fitted zones and the nation take the infection
    weighted Rt of their fitted places (`rt_observation.group_rt`),
    draw by draw, so every level comes from joint draws. Fits of
    provinces on their own pair draws by index, as their samples do.
    Places outside the fits (silent ones) have no Rt, and so add nothing
    to their province or the nation. A location and week with no
    infections in some draw has no row.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task: its `target_end_dates` are the weeks, by week of
        infection.
    runs : mapping
        `RenewalRun`s whose draws hold `weekly_rt` output (`rt`).

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `location`, `target_end_date`, `output_type_id` (`RT_QUANTILES`)
        and `value`.
    """
    from nowcastrenewal.model.rt_observation import group_rt

    weekly = [run.draws["rt"] for run in runs.values()]
    places = [name for run in runs.values() for name in run.data.names]
    n = min(w["rt"].shape[0] for w in weekly)
    codes: list[str] = []
    for place in places:
        code: str | None = place
        while code is not None:
            if code not in codes:
                codes.append(code)
            code = parent(code)

    def within(place: str, code: str) -> bool:
        while place != code and parent(place) is not None:
            place = str(parent(place))
        return place == code

    members = np.array([[within(p, c) for p in places] for c in codes])
    out: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for date in task.target_end_dates:
        rt, weight = [], []
        for w in weekly:
            i = (epiweek_end(date) - (w["start"] + dt.timedelta(days=6))).days
            k, p = i // 7, w["rt"].shape[2]
            if 0 <= k < w["rt"].shape[1]:
                rt.append(w["rt"][:n, k])
                weight.append(w["weight"][:n, k])
            else:
                rt.append(np.full((n, p), np.nan))
                weight.append(np.zeros((n, p)))
        draws = np.asarray(
            group_rt(np.hstack(rt), np.hstack(weight), members), dtype=float
        )
        keep = np.isfinite(draws).all(axis=0)
        levels = np.quantile(draws[:, keep], RT_QUANTILES, axis=0)
        kept = [c for c, k in zip(codes, keep, strict=True) if k]
        out.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "location": np.repeat(kept, len(RT_QUANTILES)),
                    "target_end_date": date,
                    "output_type_id": np.tile(RT_QUANTILES, len(kept)),
                    "value": levels.T.reshape(-1),
                }
            )
        )
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True)

def fit_renewal(
    task: ForecastTask,
    sampler: Mapping[str, Any],
    fit_dir: Path | str,
    *,
    variant: str,
    config_name: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fit a variant for the CI and write the fit directory.

    The variant is the registered model, so `renewal` and `renewalbvd`
    fit health zones (`nowcastrenewal.zones`) and also write their
    zone samples.
    Trajectories are drawn here, so `forecast_renewal` only reads them.
    Writes `samples.csv.gz`, `delay-summary.csv`, `trajectories.json`
    and `ppc.json`. `run_fit` writes the returned record to
    `diagnostics.json`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.
    sampler : mapping
        The candidate's sampler table from
        `packages/bdbvsubmission/policy.toml`.
    fit_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The fit directory.
    variant : str
        Key in `VARIANTS`.
    config_name : str
        The fit configuration, for the records.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The `diagnostics.json` record (schema 1, with `worst_rhat`, and
        `bvd`, the BVDOutbreakSize release used, for a variant with the
        BVD term).
    """
    out = Path(fit_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    settings = sampler_settings(sampler)
    seeded = replace(task, seed=int(settings.get("seed", task.seed)))
    registered = get_model(variant)
    if not isinstance(registered, RenewalModel):
        raise TypeError(f"{variant} is not a renewal model.")
    model = replace(registered, sampler=settings, progress=out / "progress.log")
    model.forecast(seeded)
    return model.write_fit_dir(seeded, out, config_name)

def write_fit_dir(
    fit: RenewalFit,
    task: ForecastTask,
    settings: Mapping[str, Any],
    fit_dir: Path | str,
    *,
    variant: str,
    config_name: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Write a fit's directory, as `forecast_renewal` reads it.

    Writes `samples.csv.gz`, `delay-summary.csv`, `trajectory_draw.csv`,
    `trajectories.json` and `ppc.json`.
    `fit_renewal` and the fit store (`RenewalModel.write_fit_dir`) both
    write a fit this way.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fit : RenewalFit
        The fit.
    task : ForecastTask
        The task it was fitted to.
    settings : mapping
        The NUTS settings it ran with (`sampler_settings`).
    fit_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The fit directory.
    variant : str
        Key in `VARIANTS`.
    config_name : str
        The fit configuration, for the records.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The `diagnostics.json` record (schema 1, with `worst_rhat`, and
        `bvd`, the BVDOutbreakSize release used, for a variant with the
        BVD term).
    """
    from nowcasteval.ppc import summarise_draws, write_ppc

    out = Path(fit_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # Only the sample columns: the backtest adds `as_of` to the samples
    # a forecast returns.
    write_csv(fit.samples.loc[:, list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS)], out / SAMPLES_FILE)
    write_csv(fit_delays(fit, task), out / DELAY_SUMMARY_FILE)
    if fit.runs:
        write_csv(rt_quantiles(task, fit.runs), out / RT_FILE)
    pairs = [
        pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "location": key,
                "sample": np.arange(1, len(run.draws["draw"]) + 1),
                "draw": np.asarray(run.draws["draw"], dtype=int),
            }
        )
        for key, run in fit.runs.items()
        if "draw" in run.draws
    ]
    if pairs:
        write_csv(
            pd.concat(pairs, ignore_index=True), out / TRAJECTORY_DRAW_FILE
        )
    modelled = sorted({c for c in fit.samples["location"] if not is_zone(c)})
    (out / TRAJECTORIES_FILE).write_text(
        json.dumps({"variant": variant, "modelled": modelled}, indent=1) + "\n"
    )
    by_run = [
        ppc_rows(run.data, run.draws["insample"]) for run in fit.runs.values()
    ]
    write_ppc(
        summarise_draws(
            pd.concat([obs for obs, _ in by_run], ignore_index=True),
            np.column_stack([dr for _, dr in by_run]),
            as_of=task.vintage,
            model=HUB_MODEL,
            config=config_name,
        ),
        out / "ppc.json",
    )
    depth = int(settings["max_tree_depth"])
    several = len(fit.runs) > 1
    params: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    chains: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for key, run in fit.runs.items():
        prefix = f"{key}:" if several else ""
        for row in parameter_diagnostics(run.trace):
            params.append({**row, "name": prefix + row["name"]})
        for row in chain_diagnostics(run.extra, depth):
            extra = {"location": key} if several else {}
            chains.append({**row, **extra, "chain": len(chains)})
    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "model": HUB_MODEL,
        "config": config_name,
        "variant": variant,
        "sampler": "nuts",
        "num_chains": len(chains),
        "num_samples": chains[0]["draws"] if chains else 0,
        "max_tree_depth": depth,
        "sampling_seconds": round(sum(r.seconds for r in fit.runs.values()), 1),
        "sampling_cpu_seconds": round(
            sum(r.cpu_seconds for r in fit.runs.values()), 1
        ),
        "parameters": params,
        "chains": chains,
        "worst_rhat": worst_rhat(params),
    }
    if model_config(VARIANTS[variant]).bvd:
        # The BVDOutbreakSize release behind the BVD term and its R-hat.
        used = [r.bvd for r in fit.runs.values() if r.bvd is not None]
        record["bvd"] = dict(used[0]) if used else bvd_record(None)
    return record

def forecast_renewal(task: ForecastTask, fit_dir: Path | str) -> Forecast:
    """Read the trajectories `fit_renewal` saved.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.
    fit_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The fit directory.

    Returns
    -------
    nowcastutils.forecast.Forecast
        Province samples and the reported provinces.
    """
    path = Path(fit_dir)
    samples = pd.read_csv(path / SAMPLES_FILE, dtype={"target_end_date": str})
    samples = samples.loc[
        samples["target_end_date"].isin(task.target_end_dates)
    ]
    meta = json.loads((path / TRAJECTORIES_FILE).read_text())
    return Forecast(
        samples=samples.reset_index(drop=True),
        modelled=tuple(meta["modelled"]),
    )

@dataclass
class ZoneRenewalModel(RenewalModel):
    """A renewal variant fitted on health zones, as a `ForecastModel`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    zone_samples : pandas.DataFrame or None
        Zone samples of the last `forecast`, which sum to its province
        samples.
    """

    zone_samples: pd.DataFrame | None = field(
        init=False, default=None, repr=False, compare=False
    )

    def run(self, task: ForecastTask) -> RenewalRun:
        """Fit the zone model to a zone task and draw trajectories.

        As `RenewalModel.run`, with `zone_vintage_inputs` and
        `build_zone_model`, and the delay summaries by province. The
        zones with a recent case are fitted. The silent ones
        (`silent_zones`) are drawn with them in one forecast pass of the
        extended model (`model.zones.extend_vintage`) from the fit's
        posterior, so their infections come only through its fitted
        importation and sample k of every zone is one joint draw. The
        posterior checks and the weekly Rt are the fitted zones'.

        Raises
        ------
        ModelUnavailableError
            If every zone of the task is silent.
        """
        from nowcastrenewal.model.zones import build_zone_model, extend_vintage

        quiet_set = silent_zones(task)
        quiet = tuple(z for z in task.locations if z in quiet_set)
        fitted = tuple(z for z in task.locations if z not in quiet_set)
        if not fitted:
            raise ModelUnavailableError(
                f"{self.name}: every zone of {task.vintage} is silent."
            )
        places = _zone_places(task)
        task = replace(task, locations=fitted)

        pr = engine()
        config = model_config(self.variant)
        rows, used = None, None
        if config.bvd:
            from nowcastrenewal import bvd

            release = bvd_release(task)
            used = bvd_record(release)
            if release is not None:
                rows = bvd.model_rows(release)
                zone_rows = zone_bvd_rows(release, _zone_names(task))
                if zone_rows is not None:
                    rows = pd.concat([rows, zone_rows], ignore_index=True)
                    used = {**used, "zones": len(zone_rows)}
            self._log(f"variant={self.name} bvd={used['tag'] or 'none'}")
        data = zone_vintage_inputs(task, config, bvd=rows, receivers=quiet)
        # The same centring rule as every variant (`fit_config`).
        config = fit_config(self.variant, data)
        model = build_zone_model(data, config)
        self._log(
            f"variant={self.name} zones={data.n_provinces} sampling start"
        )
        start, cpu_start = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
        run_nuts(model, data, {"seed": task.seed, **self.sampler})
        np.asarray(next(iter(model.mcmc.get_samples().values())))
        seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        cpu_seconds = time.process_time() - cpu_start
        self._log(
            f"variant={self.name} sampling done seconds={seconds:.0f} "
            f"cpu_seconds={cpu_seconds:.0f}"
        )
        ext = extend_vintage(data, quiet, places)
        sampled = {
            k: v
            for k, v in model.mcmc.get_samples().items()
            if k in model.mcmc.last_state.z
        }
        traj = pr.forecast_trajectories(
            build_zone_model(ext, config),
            ext,
            task.n_samples,
            seed=task.seed,
            posterior=sampled,
            as_of=tuple(report_cutoffs(task, ext)),
        )
        # The posterior checks are the fitted zones' (the first columns).
        p = len(data.names)
        draws = {
            **traj,
            "insample": {k: v[..., :p] for k, v in traj["insample"].items()},
            "rt": pr.weekly_rt(model, data, seed=task.seed),
        }
        # Each province's delay, which its zones share, and the shared one.
        trace, extra, delay = run_records(model, data, data.parent_names)
        return RenewalRun(
            self.variant,
            data,
            draws,
            trace,
            extra,
            seconds,
            cpu_seconds,
            delay,
            used,
            forecast_data=ext,
        )

    def fit_inputs(self, task: ForecastTask) -> str:
        """Hash the zone data a fit of `task` reads beside the task.

        The daily zone onsets of every release up to the task's vintage
        in its provinces, the zones it forecasts (`task_zones`) and, for
        a BVD variant, the zone names matched to the release's zone
        estimates. The fit key holds it (`bdbvhub.store.store.fit_key`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            A province task.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256.
        """
        import hashlib

        from nowcastutils.hierarchy import province_of

        daily = _zone_daily(task)
        mine = daily.loc[
            (daily["vintage"].astype(str) <= task.vintage)
            & daily["location"].map(province_of).isin(task.locations)
        ]
        digest = hashlib.sha256(mine.to_csv(index=False).encode())
        digest.update(repr(_zones_of(task)).encode())
        if model_config(self.variant).bvd:
            digest.update(_zone_names(task).to_csv(index=False).encode())
        return digest.hexdigest()[:16]

    def forecast_fit(self, task: ForecastTask) -> ZoneRenewalFit:
        """Fit the zones together and sum them to the provinces.

        The zones with a case in the random walks' walk window are
        fitted in one model, and the silent ones are drawn with them from
        its posterior, taking infections only through its fitted
        importation (`run`). Each province sample is
        the sum of its zones' samples of the same id. National is the
        sum of the provinces, and a task with national cases in no
        province stops (`check_national`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            A province task of a real release.

        Returns
        -------
        ZoneRenewalFit
            The run, province samples and zone samples.

        Raises
        ------
        ModelUnavailableError
            For a simulated task, which has no zone data.
        """
        if task.kind != "real":
            raise ModelUnavailableError(
                f"{self.name} fits the hub's zone data, which a "
                f"{task.kind} task does not have."
            )
        check_national(task)
        zt = replace(task, target=zone_target(task), locations=task_zones(task))
        runs = self._run_all({"all": zt})
        run = runs["all"]
        zone_samples = samples_table(zt, run.places, run.draws)
        later = _as_reported(zt, run)
        # The samples hold the zones too, so the forecast, the store and
        # the scores read the zone fit's own zones.
        return ZoneRenewalFit(
            runs,
            pd.concat(
                [sum_zones(zone_samples), zone_samples[list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS)]],
                ignore_index=True,
            ),
            as_reported=sum_zones(pd.concat(later, ignore_index=True))
            if later
            else None,
            zones=zone_samples,
        )

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return province samples, keeping the zone samples.

        As `RenewalModel.forecast`, and sets `zone_samples`.
        """
        out = super().forecast(task)
        fit = self.last_fit
        self.zone_samples = getattr(fit, "zones", None)
        return out

    def write_fit_dir(
        self, task: ForecastTask, fit_dir: Path | str, config_name: str
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Write the last fit's directory, with `ZONES_FILE`.

        As `RenewalModel.write_fit_dir`, plus the zone samples, which the
        submission takes in place of a split of the provinces.
        """
        record = super().write_fit_dir(task, fit_dir, config_name)
        if self.zone_samples is not None:
            write_csv(
                self.zone_samples.loc[:, list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS)],
                Path(fit_dir) / ZONES_FILE,
            )
        return record

@dataclass
class SingleZoneRenewalModel(ZoneRenewalModel):
    """A single-patch variant fitted to each zone on its own.

    Each zone with a case in the random walks' walk window is fitted with
    the single-patch model on its own series (`RenewalModel.run` on the
    zone). The silent zones take
    `randomwalknowcast`'s introductions (`_silent_walk`), as in
    `renewalsp`. Provinces are the sums of their zones, sample by sample,
    and national is their sum, so no province sample is split across
    zones. Zone fits pair draws by index, as `renewalsp`'s provinces do.
    """

    def run(self, task: ForecastTask) -> RenewalRun:
        """Fit one zone on its own (`RenewalModel.run`)."""
        return RenewalModel.run(self, task)

    def forecast_fit(self, task: ForecastTask) -> ZoneRenewalFit:
        """Fit each zone with a recent case on its own and sum them.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            A province task of a real release.

        Returns
        -------
        ZoneRenewalFit
            The runs by zone, province samples and zone samples.

        Raises
        ------
        ModelUnavailableError
            For a simulated task, which has no zone data.
        """
        if task.kind != "real":
            raise ModelUnavailableError(
                f"{self.name} fits the hub's zone data, which a "
                f"{task.kind} task does not have."
            )
        check_national(task)
        walk, silent = _silent_walk(_zone_walk_task(task))
        target = zone_target(task)
        fitted = tuple(z for z in task_zones(task) if z not in silent)
        tasks = {
            z: replace(task, target=target, locations=(z,), mask=())
            for z in fitted
        }
        runs = self._run_all(tasks)
        frames = [walk]
        later = [
            walk.loc[walk["target_end_date"] <= d].assign(as_of=d)
            for d in task.report_by
        ]
        for key, run in runs.items():
            frames.append(samples_table(tasks[key], run.data, run.draws))
            later.extend(_as_reported(tasks[key], run))
        zone_samples = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
        return ZoneRenewalFit(
            runs,
            pd.concat(
                [sum_zones(zone_samples), zone_samples[list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS)]],
                ignore_index=True,
            ),
            as_reported=sum_zones(pd.concat(later, ignore_index=True))
            if later
            else None,
            zones=zone_samples,
        )

def task_zones(task: ForecastTask) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return the health zones of a task's provinces.

    The task's zone codes (`ForecastTask.zone_codes`, the hub's codes),
    which its forecast is checked against.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        A province task.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of str
        Zone codes, sorted.

    Raises
    ------
    ModelUnavailableError
        If the task holds no zone codes (a task built without zone data).
    """
    if not task.zone_codes:
        raise ModelUnavailableError(
            "A zone fit needs the task's zone codes; build the task with "
            "the zone data (`load_zone_data`)."
        )
    return _zones_of(task)
